issues.title: Three new cli tests need `claude` on PATH - they fail on any clean machine and break the release CI gate
issues.description: cli/go_plan_readiness_test.go's `TestCmdGoRefusesAcceptedButUnwrittenPlan` (both subtests) and `TestCmdGoAuthoringHintReachesTheUser` call cmdGo without stubbing `claude`. cmdGo checks `launch.HasClaude()` (cli/go.go:130) BEFORE it loads the repo, so on a host without the claude binary the command exits 1 with "gogo go: claude CLI not on PATH" and every assertion about the FR8 refusal / authoring hint fails. Verified: `env PATH="$(dirname $(which go)):/usr/bin:/bin" go test ./...` in cli/ fails with exactly these 3 tests (4 with subtests) and NOTHING else - the rest of the suite is hermetic, so this is a new regression in hermeticity. .github/workflows/release.yml runs `go test -race ./...` on ubuntu-latest as "the one gate: the CLI suite must be green before anything is published"; claude is not installed there, so tagging v0.29.0 fails the gate and publishes no binaries. It also breaks coding-rules.md's non-negotiable `go test -race ./...` gate for any other contributor. Note the sibling test `TestCmdGoRunsAWrittenPlan` deliberately sets PATH to an empty dir, which is what made the asymmetry easy to miss.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Use the package's existing hermetic seam, the way go_cap_test.go does: `binDir := writeStubClaude(t)` + `t.Setenv("PATH", binDir+string(os.PathListSeparator)+os.Getenv("PATH"))` (or a minimal `t.Setenv("PATH", dirWithExecutableNamedClaude)`) at the top of both tests, so the refusal is reached because of the plan gate and not skipped by the PATH guard. Then re-verify with `env PATH="$(dirname $(which go)):/usr/bin:/bin" go test ./...` in cli/ - it must be green with no claude anywhere on PATH. Keep TestCmdGoRunsAWrittenPlan as is (its empty PATH is the intended next-guard proof).
issues.fix_summary: Both cmdGo tests now wire the package's hermetic seam (writeStubClaude + wireStub) before calling cmdGo, so the FR8 refusal is reached because of the plan gate rather than skipped by the claude-on-PATH guard. Strengthened while there: each subtest also asserts the stub was never exec'd (no argv.log) and that no owner-lock dir was created, which pins FR8's 'refuses BEFORE launch and before the lock' property. Verified with `env PATH="$(dirname $(which go)):/usr/bin:/bin" go test ./...` - the whole suite is green with no claude anywhere on PATH - and the hermetic run is now part of the gate I run every time. Mutation R01 (revert to the pre-fix shape) reproduces exactly the reviewer's 3 failures.

issues.title: FR12a incomplete: three live user-visible copies of the OLD cap rule still say "in-progress work items with a live session"
issues.description: FR12 changed what the cap counts; FR12a requires every user-visible statement of the rule to move with it ("or the most legible message in the cockpit becomes the most wrong") and explicitly names the help text. The bounce (cli/internal/tui/move.go:221), cap.go's doc comment, README.md and skills/gogo-cli/SKILL.md were updated, but three live surfaces were not: (1) cli/main.go:204 - `gogo --help`: "0 = unlimited; N caps THAT source's in-progress work items that have a live session."; (2) cli/internal/tui/config_tab.go:117 - the source-edit form field Description the user reads while SETTING the cap: "N caps THIS source's in-progress work items that have a live session ..."; (3) cli/internal/tui/config_tab.go:479 `capScopeNote` - the source-detail line "(this source only . counts in-progress work items with a live session . plans never count)". Their doc comments (config_tab.go:114-116, 474-477) repeat the stale rule too. All three are now factually wrong: a mid-build item reading `plan-accepted` is ClassUnfinished and IS counted. 0.28.0 deliberately wrote this rule in four places (bounce, config form, source detail, --help); only the bounce moved. Review standard #1 (cross-file enumeration sync) and the plan's own build-note claim ("two additional FR12a copies ... found and updated") are both unmet.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Replace the three copies with the sentence already shipped in the bounce, e.g. "N caps THIS source's work items that have a live BUILD session (gogo-go-<slug>) - authoring/plan sessions and plans are never counted", and fix the two doc comments above them. Then grep for the old wording repo-wide (`grep -rn "in-progress work items with a live session"`), leaving only the dated 0.28.0 historical notes (docs/cli-contract.md:88, .gogo/knowledge/project-knowledge.md:402) which are release history, not current copy. Consider extending an existing test to assert the config-tab/help strings state the new rule, as authoring_test.go's TestCapBounceStatesTheNewRule already does for the bounce.
issues.fix_summary: Root-caused rather than re-copied: the rule is now ONE constant, orchestrator.CapRuleClause, quoted by all four surfaces that state it (gogo --help, the config-tab cap field, capScopeNote, the board bounce). Hand-copying is what let 3 of 4 go stale, so single-sourcing makes that drift impossible instead of merely forbidden. Three durable guards added in cli/cap_rule_test.go: every surface must reference the constant; no production .go file may contain any pre-0.29.0 phrasing (a repo-wide walk); and the constant itself must name the build session, the per-source scope and what is not counted. The grep guard immediately found a FOURTH stale copy the review had not listed - capBounce's own doc comment ('in-progress+live features') - which is now fixed too. Search method: `grep -rn` over *.go/*.md/*.json for four phrasings ('in-progress work items with a live session', '...that have a live session', 'in-progress features that carry a live', 'in-progress+live'); the only remaining hits are dated 0.28.0 release-history notes (docs/cli-contract.md:88, .gogo/knowledge/project-knowledge.md) and this work item's own decisions/review records, which are history, not current copy.

issues.title: FR8's refusal is missing on the reload AUTO-PICKUP path - the one launch path with no human in the loop
issues.description: FR8 is enforced on the board's m/M (tui/move.go planReadinessBounce) and on `gogo go` (cli/go.go), but not on the third launch path in the same package: the fsnotify-reload auto-pickup. `autoPickupReady` (cli/internal/tui/pickup.go:33-45) gates on correlation + `status == "plan-accepted"` + skip-source + no live session, and never consults `f.PlanUnwritten`. Verified with a throwaway probe against a copy of the tree (member("web-token",...,"plan-accepted") with PlanUnwritten=true, PlanAcceptanceSkip source): `autoPickupReady=true`, `autoPickupCmds()` returns 1 cmd and the fake launcher records `"/gogo:go web-token --skip-acceptance"`. That is an UNATTENDED build launched at a folder with no plan in it - exactly the aggravating case the plan's own Context calls out ("in a planAcceptanceSkip source the reload auto-pickup has already fired `claude -p /gogo:go <slug>` at it unattended"), and it is reachable by precisely the failure mode this feature exists to fix (an analyst writing state.md before plan.md, with the plan gate auto-accepted by the source's skip flag). The only thing left between it and a build is gogo-implement's new prose gate - i.e. LLM prose guarding LLM prose, which is the pattern the plan's Approach section rejects. The human path is correctly refused on the same card (footer reads `[m] x plan not written`, `m` bounces), which makes the automated hole the asymmetry to close.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add the deterministic guard to `autoPickupReady`: after the status check, `if f.PlanUnwritten { return false }` with a comment naming FR8 (an unwritten plan is not an auto-pickup candidate; it is not blocked by a cap, it is illegal). Both the fire path and the `autoPickupBlocked` cue share the helper, so the card falls back to the plan-not-written cue instead of a misleading "trigger manually". Add a test in pickup_test.go asserting `autoPickupCmds()` returns NO cmd and the fake launcher fires ZERO times for a plan-accepted member with `PlanUnwritten: true` (and that a written-plan member still fires exactly once, so the guard bites only on the defect).
issues.fix_summary: autoPickupReady now returns false when f.PlanUnwritten, right after the status check, with a comment naming FR8 and why the unattended path must be at least as strict as the human one. Because the fire path and the blocked-cue path share the helper, the card falls back to the plan-not-written cue instead of the misleading 'trigger manually'. TestAutoPickupRefusesAnUnwrittenPlan asserts BOTH arms so the guard is proven to bite only on the defect: zero cmds, zero launcher calls, nothing recorded in the fire-once set, autoPickupBlocked false and planReadinessBounce non-empty for the unwritten member; and an otherwise-identical WRITTEN member still fires exactly one /gogo:go. Also corrected the shared on-disk fixture (writePlanAcceptedMember) to write a real plan.md - it stood in for an accepted plan while having none, which is the defect, not a fixture.

issues.title: cap_test.go's surviving comments still document the deleted `Class` filter as if it were under test
issues.description: cli/internal/orchestrator/cap_test.go keeps three statements of the removed rule: the TestActiveWorkCount doc comment ("it counts a root's DISTINCT in-progress features that carry a live gogo-* session"), the fixture line `feat("ready", root, contract.ClassReadyToShip), // wrong class -> not counted` (line 24) and TestActiveWorkParkedNotCounted's "(the count is in-progress ^ live)". After FR12 the class is no longer why `ready` is not counted - it is not counted because no session in the fixture attributes to it. Review standard #11 says to flag a test whose comment claims coverage its assertions do not provide: a reader (or a future mutator) will believe class filtering is still pinned here. The assertions themselves are correct and still pass.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Reword the three comments to the new rule: the count is "features with a live BUILD session, per root, distinct, excluding the target"; annotate the `ready` fixture line as "no session -> not counted (its class is irrelevant since 0.29.0)"; and either give `ready` a `gogo-done-ready` session so the line proves the ACTION test, or delete the stale parenthetical. No production change.
issues.fix_summary: All three comments reworded to the new rule (the count is 'features with a live BUILD session, per root, distinct, excluding the target'), and the `ready` fixture row was made LOAD-BEARING rather than just re-annotated: it now carries a gogo-done-ready session, and the test asserts both that the session IS attributed to the slug and that liveBuildSession is false for it - so the row proves the ACTION test instead of merely not being counted. The subtests now assert the exact returned SLUGS, not just the tally, since a count alone cannot distinguish 'counted alpha+beta' from 'counted alpha+ready'. Mutation R09 (removing that session) survived the first sweep, which is what showed the annotation alone was not coverage.

issues.title: The drill-in note is asserted on `Model.status` only, not in `viewDrill()` output - the exact shape review standard #8 says to flag
issues.description: TestQuickViewNamesTheMissingPlan (cli/internal/tui/authoring_test.go:485) asserts `got.status`, `got.statusLevel` and `got.mode`, but never `got.View()`. Standard #8 / test-strategy TEST (0.16.0 drill-card finding) is explicit: "flag ... a test that asserts only Model.status (not the View() output) for such a path - that gap shipped a silent no-op once (the drill-card status line)", and the drill-in status line is literally that path. I verified by probe against a copy that the note DOES render today (viewDrill renders `m.renderStatus(m.status)`, and a probe found both "plan.md not written yet" and the warn glyph in the rendered output), so this is a coverage gap rather than a live no-op - but it is the one new user-visible string in this change whose render is unguarded, and every other new string in the diff (bounce, footer chip, cues, header count) is asserted in View().
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Extend TestQuickViewNamesTheMissingPlan with `out := got.View()` and assert `strings.Contains(out, statusWarnMarker)` plus the reason and the unblock ("plan.md not written yet", "gogo plan demo"), the same way TestAuthoringMoveBounceIsBlockedSeverityAndRendered does for the board mode. No production change.
issues.fix_summary: TestQuickViewNamesTheMissingPlan now asserts got.View(): the warn glyph, the reason clause and the unblock must all appear in the rendered drill output, the same way the board-mode test does. Mutation R10 (deleting the setStatus call from quickView) is caught by it.

issues.title: FR11's entry-write was skipped on its very first live run: this review round is executing with state.md still reading implement/implementing
issues.description: The three phase skills gained a separate `## (1)b Enter the phase` section between validate-in and (2) Steps. gogo-review's own copy says "Your FIRST act after validate-in passes, before you read the diff: write state.md phase: review + status: reviewing, and append the phase-started line". At the time this review ran, .gogo/work/feature-plan-readiness-gate/state.md read `phase: implement` / `status: implementing` and events.jsonl's last line was implement's `phase-done` (00:06) - no review `phase-started`. So the first phase to run under the new rule (review, this round) did not honour it, while implement DID (entry 23:22, done 00:06, 44 min apart - FR11 demonstrably works there). That matters for two reasons: code-review-standards #5 requires state.md to be kept current at transitions, and the plan's own thesis is that a writer instruction which sits outside the numbered flow is the class of instruction that already failed once. The reader-side guards do NOT cover this case: the cap and the `- building` cue key on a live `gogo-go` session, which is present for the whole warm run, so nothing on the board reveals that the phase line lags by a phase (D6=A deliberately keeps the file-derived column).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE (prose). Fold the entry write into the numbered flow instead of a sibling section: make it step 1 of `## (2) Steps` ("1. Record occupancy: write phase/status + append phase-started - before anything else") in gogo-implement / gogo-review / gogo-test, keeping the rationale paragraph beneath it, and mirror the same shape in skills/gogo/SKILL.md's in-context path. Optionally have gogo-contracts' validate-in return the occupancy write as its final act, so passing the gate and recording it are one step. Also record in the (5) report that FR11's writer half is advisory and was observed skipped once, so the release does not over-claim "the board no longer narrates the past" for (3)/(4).
issues.fix_summary: Accepted as evidence and answered on both halves. PROSE: the entry write moved out of the sibling `## (1)b` section into step 1 of the numbered `## (2) Steps` flow in gogo-implement/review/test (an instruction outside the numbered steps is one that gets skipped), with skills/gogo/SKILL.md's in-context path and the telemetry section updated to match. DETERMINISTIC READER GUARD - the part that actually holds: contract.Feature.LatestEvent already carries the newest events.jsonl line, so tui.phaseLineLags reports the lag when the newest event is a `phase-done` for the very phase state.md still names AND a build session is live; the card then reads `· state lags`. That is precisely the case the other cues cannot see, because the warm gogo-go session is live for all of 2/3/4/5. Guarded by TestPhaseLineLagsCue with six negative cases (entry write honoured, phase-started not phase-done, awaiting-uat after report's phase-done, no session, no events.jsonl, an authoring-only session) plus the knowledge->report mapping. Recorded honestly in plan.md and docs/flow.md: the release claims the board no longer narrates the past for phase 2, and that for 3/4/5 it either narrates the present or SAYS OUT LOUD that it cannot.

issues.title: The render path now opens plan.md every frame just to test a boolean
issues.description: footerChips (cli/internal/tui/view.go:824) decides the `[m]` chip with `planReadinessBounce(f) != ""`. planReadinessBounce calls contract.PlanUnwrittenReason(f.Dir), which os.Opens and scans plan.md, and then formats a full refusal sentence - all discarded except for the emptiness test. It runs on every View() for a focused ClassUnfinished card (keystrokes, fsnotify reloads, the plans-tab redraws), even though the answer is already on the Feature: `f.PlanUnwritten` is derived once per load by loadFeature. Small in absolute terms (one open + an early-exit scan) and not a violation of the read-path NFR, but it puts avoidable syscalls and garbage in a render path, and it makes the render answer depend on disk state that can differ from the loaded model's - the kind of split the plan otherwise works hard to avoid (one source of truth per read).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add a pure predicate next to planReadinessBounce, e.g. `func planUnready(f *contract.Feature) bool { return f != nil && (f.Authoring() || (f.Status == "plan-accepted" && f.PlanUnwritten)) }`, and use it in footerChips and as the branch in planColumnViewNote; keep planReadinessBounce (which quotes PlanUnwrittenReason) for the keystroke paths that actually show the sentence. Assert the two agree in a small test so they cannot drift.
issues.fix_summary: Added the pure predicate tui.planUnready(f) - no I/O, no formatting - and used it in footerChips (the render path) and as the branch in planColumnViewNote; planReadinessBounce (which quotes PlanUnwrittenReason and so reads plan.md) stays for the keystroke paths that actually display the sentence. TestPlanUnreadyAgreesWithTheBounce pins the two in step across seven cases so they cannot drift. The no-I/O property itself is asserted STRUCTURALLY, because it cannot be asserted behaviourally: both forms answer off the same model fields, so swapping them changes no output - a mutation confirmed the behavioural version of the test survived that exact revert. TestFooterChipDoesNoDiskIO now reads footerChips' source (comments stripped, so a guard reads code rather than prose) and fails if it reaches for planReadinessBounce.

issues.title: Dropping the Class filter also lets a TERMINAL feature consume a cap slot - intended by D5=A, but untested and undocumented
issues.description: ActiveWorkSlugs now skips only nil / other-root / excluded / no-build-session, so a feature at `shipped`/`done` (ClassShipped) whose `gogo-go-<slug>` session is still alive is counted, where the old class filter always excluded it. That direction is sanctioned by the plan ("counts a feature in root that has a live go session, regardless of its file-derived class") and is arguably correct - a live claude session in that tree is the clobber risk the cap names - but nothing pins it: TestCapCountsOnlyBuildSessions only proves that non-`go` actions do not count, and cap.go's rewritten doc comment enumerates parked / authoring / accept / done / author / resume without mentioning the terminal-class case. So a future reader cannot tell intent from oversight, and if /gogo:done's best-effort targeted ship-reap fails (skills/gogo-done/SKILL.md:288 swallows errors) the source stays capped by a shipped item's leftover session with no explanation on the board.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Decide once and pin it: add a case to TestCapCountsOnlyBuildSessions (or a new test) with a `{Slug: "shipped", Class: ClassShipped, Status: "shipped"}` feature plus a live `gogo-go-shipped` session, asserting the intended answer, and add one sentence to cap.go's doc comment stating it ("a terminal feature still holding a live build session IS counted - the session, not the class, is the clobber risk; the ship-reap is what normally removes it"). If the intended answer is 'not counted', gate on `!orchestrator.TerminalStatus(f.Status)` instead - but then say so, because it re-introduces a file-derived condition.
issues.fix_summary: Decided and pinned: a terminal feature still holding a live BUILD session IS counted. Review standard #9 records that 'reaping a terminal feature's session is safe by definition' is false, so a live gogo-go session in that tree is a real claude editing a real working tree - the clobber risk the cap names - and gating on !TerminalStatus would put a file-derived condition back into the one guard FR12 made deterministic. cap.go's doc comment now states this, names how it clears (/gogo:done's ship-reap, else `gogo sweep`), and TestCapCountsATerminalFeatureStillHoldingABuildSession pins all three arms (counted with a live go session, not counted once reaped, not counted for a gogo-done session). Consequence handled rather than just documented: the cap bounce now also names `gogo sweep` as an unblock, since 'ship one' is useless advice when the blocker is an already-shipped item's leftover session.

issues.title: The `state lags` detector only sees FORWARD hand-offs: a fix-round re-entry with a stale phase line is invisible
issues.description: `phaseLineLags` (cli/internal/tui/model.go) requires the newest event to be a `phase-done` for the phase state.md names. That covers the forward hand-offs (2->3, 3->4, 4->5) but not the pipeline's most common re-entry, the loop BACK to implement, nor a partial step-1 where the event landed and the state.md write did not. Two probe-verified blind spots, both with a live build session: (a) review found issues, implement re-entered with --issues and appended its `fix-round`/implement entry event but skipped the occupancy write, so state.md still reads review/reviewing while implement edits code -> phaseLineLags=false, cue ""; (b) a phase appended `phase-started`/review while state.md still reads implement/implementing (the event half of step 1 done, the state half skipped) -> phaseLineLags=false, cue "". Both are exactly the failure REV-006 exists to make visible, and in both the telemetry NAMES the newer phase - stronger evidence than the phase-done shape the detector does check. Note the review skill's `issues-found` event is not a phase-end marker, so the round-01 shape that WAS observed live trips the detector only because review skipped its telemetry too; an agent that emits its events but skips the state write stays invisible.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add the symmetric arm: an ENTRY event (`phase-started` or `fix-round`) whose `phase` is not `contract.EventsPhase(f.Phase)`, with a live build session and no user gate, also means the phase line is behind - the event says work moved to X while state.md still says Y. Keep the existing phase-done arm (it catches the hand-off where no entry event was emitted at all). Extend TestPhaseLineLagsCue with the two shapes above as POSITIVE cases, plus a negative case for an entry event that MATCHES state.md's phase (the healthy mid-phase shape). The cue text is unchanged, so the only doc touch is skills/gogo-cli's one-line description of when it fires.
issues.fix_summary: Generalised, but to the PRECISE rule rather than the broadest one. phaseLineLags now has two arms: (A) the existing `phase-done` for the phase state.md names - the forward hand-off nothing claimed; (B) an ENTRY event (`phase-started`/`fix-round`) whose phase differs from the line - which catches both shapes the review found (the fix-round re-entry with a stale phase line, and the partial step 1 where the event landed and the state write did not). Deliberately NOT "any event whose phase disagrees": a mid-phase event left over from an earlier phase (issues-found/review after implement correctly re-entered AND wrote its state) is ordinary telemetry lag, which docs/cli-contract.md §5 calls normal - flagging it would report a lag on a writer that did everything right. That boundary is now a negative test case of its own, and mutation A07 (widening arm B to any event) is caught by it. Three positive shapes added to TestPhaseLineLagsCue including the knowledge/report mapping; verified live - the fix-round probe card renders `reviewing · ● reviewer · state lags`.

issues.title: `phaseLineLags` has no status whitelist, so a terminal feature with a lingering build session reads `· state lags`
issues.description: Its sibling `stalledPhase` whitelists the three working statuses; `phaseLineLags` accepts ANY status that is not a user gate. Probe: a feature with `status: aborted`, `phase: implement`, newest event `phase-done`/implement and a live `gogo-go-demo` session renders `· state lags` - nothing is lagging, the item is terminal. Reachability is narrow but it is precisely REV-008's scenario (a build session that outlived a failed ship-reap), and an aborted item whose phase is implement/review/test classifies ClassInProgress, so it renders as a real card. `status: shipped` escapes only incidentally (ClassShipped -> the collapsed changelog list, which never calls renderCard), so today's protection is a rendering accident rather than a rule.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Mirror stalledPhase and gate on the status: return false unless `f.Status` is one of the working statuses the entry write is supposed to have set (implementing / reviewing / testing) - or equivalently `if orchestrator.TerminalStatus(f.Status) { return false }` (the tui package already imports orchestrator in move.go). Add the aborted + lingering-session shape as a seventh negative case in TestPhaseLineLagsCue.
issues.fix_summary: Added the working-status whitelist, mirroring stalledPhase: phaseLineLags returns false unless status is implementing/reviewing/testing. It subsumes the previous user-gate check (awaiting-uat/waiting-for-user are not working statuses), so it is now the single status rule rather than two overlapping ones. Two negative cases added (aborted and shipped, each with a lingering build session). Note this whitelist also made REV-013's overlap unreachable - see that entry.

issues.title: The cap bounce now recommends the WHOLE-BOARD `gogo sweep`, which reaps other sources' live builds as orphans
issues.description: REV-008's fix added a remedy to the board's cap bounce (cli/internal/tui/move.go:244): "press M to force, ship one, run `gogo sweep` if a blocker already shipped, or run `gogo go <slug> --force`". The remedy itself works - probe-verified: the sweep reaps the shipped blocker's session ("owning feature shipped-one is shipped") and ActiveWorkSlugs then returns empty, so the slot really frees. But it names the BARE form, and the bare form is host-global: with `Sweeper.Only` empty every `gogo-*` session on the machine is judged against THIS repo's feature list, and a session belonging to another source's feature has no owning feature here, so `shouldReap` classifies it "orphan - no owning feature" and kills it. Probe: with sessions [gogo-go-shipped-one, gogo-go-someone-elses-live-build] the bare sweep killed BOTH; `gogo sweep shipped-one` killed only the blocker. `cmdSweep` has no confirmation (only an opt-in --dry-run), so acting on the advice destroys another project's in-flight build immediately. This message appears in the multi-source cockpit by construction (a per-source cap on the unified board), and the repo's own knowledge singles the bare form out as the dangerous one (test-strategy.md: "a real killing whole-board `gogo sweep` (no slug) ... can reap the user's REAL in-flight sessions"; code-review-standards #9 requires slug-targeting for reaps). In fairness the bare form IS the sanctioned MANUAL cleanup - but recommending it inline as the fix for one named blocker strips exactly the context `sweepHelp` provides, and the targeted form costs nothing because the bounce already prints the blocking slugs.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Interpolate the blocking slug(s) the bounce already has: "run `gogo sweep <slug>` if it already shipped" (for several blockers the space-separated `gogo sweep a b` is the same targeted form). Extend TestCapBounceStatesTheNewRule to assert the bounce names `gogo sweep <blocking-slug>` and does NOT offer a bare `gogo sweep` (assert the exact substring so a later re-copy cannot reintroduce it). Mirror the same remedy in cmdGo's capBlock - see REV-015.
issues.fix_summary: Fixed at the root and single-sourced: new orchestrator.CapSweepRemedy(blocking) can ONLY emit the TARGETED `gogo sweep <slug>...` (space-separated for several blockers, and "" when there is nothing to name, so it can never degrade to a bare sweep). Both cap refusals quote it - the board's capBounce and cmdGo's capBlock (REV-015) - so the two cannot drift. Guards: TestCapSweepRemedyIsAlwaysTargeted at the producer, plus assertions in TestCapBounceStatesTheNewRule and TestCapBlock that the exact targeted substring is present AND that no bare `gogo sweep` appears, so a later re-copy cannot reintroduce the destructive advice. Verified live on a multi-source probe: the bounce reads "run `gogo sweep zzshipped zzfixround` if a blocker already shipped" and the headless refusal matches. On the second question: hardening bare `gogo sweep` itself is recorded in plan.md as OUT OF SCOPE with the reasoning, not silently left - the reachable defect was that this feature RECOMMENDED the bare form, which is now impossible; making the command interactive needs its own decision about non-TTY callers (a prompt would block a headless `claude -p`), and the deeper fix is that the bare sweep judges host-wide sessions against ONE repo's feature list, so the honest repair is to resolve owners across all registered sources (projects.AllSources) rather than to confirm a misclassification.

issues.title: The cap-rule single-source guard is file-granular and comment-blind, so a partial hand-write survives the whole suite
issues.description: `TestCapRuleIsSingleSourced` (cli/cap_rule_test.go) asserts that each of the four surface FILES contains the substring "CapRuleClause", over the raw file including comments. config_tab.go carries TWO surfaces (the cap form field and capScopeNote), so re-hand-writing ONE of them still leaves the identifier in the file - in the other surface AND in three explanatory comments that name it. Mutation N11 proves it: replacing the cap field's `"..."+orchestrator.CapRuleClause` with a fresh hand-written sentence ("N caps this repo's running items" - wording absent from staleCapRulePhrases) compiles and leaves the ENTIRE suite green, so the field the user reads while setting the cap can silently go stale again - which is exactly what REV-002 was. The companion grep only catches the four known pre-0.29.0 phrasings, so any new wording passes both guards. Contrast the tui guard for the same class of property, which strips `//` comments before matching (TestFooterChipDoesNoDiskIO / tuiFuncBody): the technique needed here already exists in the repo.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Two cheap steps: (1) strip comments before matching (reuse the stripLineComments idea), or count occurrences of `orchestrator.CapRuleClause` in code and require one per surface rather than one per file; (2) prefer RENDERED assertions over file greps for the two config_tab surfaces, exactly as TestHelpStatesTheCapRule does for --help - assert `capScopeNote(1)` contains `orchestrator.CapRuleClause`, and assert the source-form field's Description does too (extract it into a small `capFieldDescription()` helper and assert that, or read the field back off the built form). A rendered assertion cannot be satisfied by a comment or by a sibling surface.
issues.fix_summary: Both halves of the reviewer's proposal, because the file-granular guard had exactly the defect it was written to prevent. (1) STRUCTURAL: the guard now strips `//` comments and counts code references PER SURFACE, not per file - config_tab.go owns two, so it must reference the constant at least twice. (2) BEHAVIOURAL, which is the real backstop: capFieldDescription() was extracted as a named producer so the rendered strings can be asserted, and TestConfigTabCapSurfacesRenderTheRule (in the tui package, where the producers live - no test-only exports into production) asserts capFieldDescription() and capScopeNote(1) each contain the shared clause and no pre-0.29.0 wording. Mutations A11/A12 (hand-writing either surface with fresh wording absent from the stale-phrase list) are now caught by both guards. Scored honestly with a TWO-PART mutation (A13b: weaken the guard back to per-file AND hand-write one surface), which the behavioural test still catches - a guard-only mutation can never fail while the production code is correct, so it was not a scoreable result on its own.

issues.title: cardStateCue's documented "Order matters" is unguarded, and both predicates are simultaneously true in a reachable state
issues.description: cardStateCue's doc comment states "Order matters. `● building` comes first because it is the more specific statement of the same underlying fact". Mutation N16 swaps the `buildingDisagreement` and `phaseLineLags` arms: it compiles and the whole suite stays green, so the documented invariant is unpinned. It is not theoretical either - probe: a UAT-rerun card (`status: plan-accepted` after re-acceptance, `phase: knowledge`, newest event `phase-done`/report, live gogo-go session) makes BOTH predicates true, so the order alone decides whether the user sees `● building` (correct - it is being rebuilt) or `· state lags`. This is the review-#11a "prefer a guard that cannot be escaped" gap on a decision the code itself calls load-bearing.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add the both-true case to TestPhaseLineLagsCue (or a small TestCueOrderIsSpecificFirst): the UAT-rerun feature above must yield `● building`, asserting BOTH that buildingDisagreement and phaseLineLags are true for it (so the fixture cannot silently stop exercising the overlap) and that cardStateCue returns the building cue. That single test makes the swap fail.
issues.fix_summary: Investigated rather than patched, and the outcome is stronger than the request. The reason swapping the arms survived is that REV-010's whitelist made the two status sets DISJOINT: buildingDisagreement needs plan-accepted/awaiting-plan-acceptance, phaseLineLags needs implementing/reviewing/testing, and stalledPhase needs no live session while both others need one. So no swap CAN change behaviour, no test could ever fail on one, and the reviewer's UAT-rerun overlap fixture is no longer an overlap. The doc comment's "Order matters" was therefore itself a claim that did not hold - the same defect class - so it was replaced with the invariant that does: TestCueArmsAreMutuallyExclusive asserts over a status x phase x event x sessions cross-product that at most one arm is ever true, plus a reachability check that the matrix actually makes each arm true (or the exclusivity would be vacuous). Widening any arm into another's status set now fails that test and forces the precedence to be decided deliberately - mutation A14 confirms it, and A15 (shrinking the matrix so an arm is never reached) confirms the reachability guard bites.

issues.title: The detector's justification comments overstate what each event shape proves - arm B's is ambiguous by construction
issues.description: `phaseLineLags`'s doc comment justifies restricting arm B to entry events like this: "a mid-phase event left over from an earlier phase (issues-found/review after implement correctly re-entered and wrote its state) is just telemetry lag ... flagging it would report a lag on a feature whose writer did everything right. So the narrower rule is the precise one, not merely the safe one." The DECISION is right; the reasoning is not, in two ways. (a) In that scenario the writer did NOT do everything right - if implement had, its own `fix-round` would be the newest event, not `issues-found`; what actually happened is that implement wrote state.md and its best-effort event append did not land. The correct justification is narrower and stronger: state.md is CORRECT there, so there is no lag to report. (b) The same failure mode applies to arm B and is not excluded by it. Probe: state.md `implement`/`implementing` with newest event `phase-started`/review and a live build session fires arm B - but that on-disk shape has two readings, (i) review started and skipped its state write (lag, cue right) and (ii) implement re-entered, wrote its state and its event append failed (state correct, cue WRONG, it blames the right file for the wrong reason). They are byte-identical on disk, so no rule can separate them; the comment's claim that an entry-event disagreement "is evidence that work moved on rather than ordinary telemetry lag" is therefore too strong. Symmetrically, arm A can be MASKED: a phase that skips step 1 but later appends its mid-phase `issues-found` replaces the `phase-done` that arm A was reading, and the cue goes silent (probe-confirmed). Both residuals are acceptable - the cue still marks a real disagreement between state.md and events.jsonl - but the comment is the rationale a future maintainer will tune the rule from, and it currently promises a precision the shape cannot deliver.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, comment-only. In `phaseLineLags`: (1) restate the mid-phase exclusion as "state.md is correct in that shape - only the best-effort telemetry is behind - so there is no lag to report"; (2) add one sentence recording that arm B's shape is ambiguous (a skipped state write and a failed event append look identical on disk), so the cue means "state.md and events.jsonl disagree about the current phase - one half of step 1 did not land", which is what the user should check; (3) note that a mid-phase event can mask arm A, so silence is not proof of health. Optionally mirror sentence (2) in skills/gogo-cli's cue description. No code change - and no test change, since the negative case that pins the boundary is already there.
issues.fix_summary: Comment-only, reasoning corrected as directed. phaseLineLags now says: the mid-phase shape is excluded because `state.md` is CORRECT there - it names the phase actually running - and only the best-effort telemetry is behind, so there is no lag to report; and explicitly retracts the earlier "the writer did everything right" claim (implement's own fix-round would be the newest event if it had - the event append is what failed). Added the ambiguity: arm B's shape is byte-identical whether review skipped its state write or implement wrote its state and its append failed, so the honest reading of the cue is "state.md and events.jsonl disagree about the current phase - one half of step 1 did not land", which is what the user should check. Added that SILENCE IS NOT PROOF OF HEALTH, since a later mid-phase event can overwrite the phase-done arm A keys on. Mirrored the honest reading in skills/gogo-cli's cue description. No code or test change - the negative case that pins the boundary was already there.

issues.title: `CapSweepRemedy`'s empty return would render as double punctuation at both call sites, and its doc claims a caller contract neither call site honours
issues.description: `CapSweepRemedy` returns "" for an empty slug list, documented as "so a caller with nothing to name omits the remedy instead of emitting a bare `gogo sweep`". Neither caller omits it: both interpolate it unconditionally with a `%s` between two commas, so an empty return renders "press M to force, ship one, , or run ..." (board) and "ship/finish one first, , or re-run ..." (`gogo go`). It is UNREACHABLE today - both sites are behind `CapExceeded(cap, len(active))`, which requires `len(active) >= cap >= 1`, so `active` is never empty there - which is why this is a nit and not a defect. But the doc states a contract the code does not implement, and the empty case is exactly what a future caller (a plans-tab cap message, a `gogo status` hint) would hit first.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, either direction. Cheapest: correct the doc to say the empty case is unreachable from both current call sites and that a new caller must handle "" itself. Better: make it true - have each call site build its remedy list (e.g. append the non-empty parts and `strings.Join(parts, ", ")`) so an empty remedy simply drops out, and add a one-line test that a zero-blocker refusal has no double comma.
issues.fix_summary: Made the contract true rather than correcting the doc down to the code. New orchestrator.CapRefusal(remedies...) joins the non-empty parts, so an empty CapSweepRemedy simply drops out; both refusals compose through it. The doc now states plainly that callers must drop an empty remedy and that CapRefusal is what does it. Tests: CapRefusal drops the empty part, produces no ", ,", and is "" when everything is empty. Because the empty case is unreachable from both call sites (each sits behind CapExceeded, which needs a non-empty blocker list), the composition itself is pinned STRUCTURALLY at both sites - TestCapRefusalsComposeThroughCapRefusal (board) and TestCapBlockComposesThroughCapRefusal (headless) - after a mutation showed a silent revert to unconditional interpolation survived everything.

issues.title: The knowledge sweep is incomplete: three always-read statements still describe the REMOVED exit write, and one tells a future reviewer to flag the restoration

Then re-grep for `stay at the exit` / `no longer sets` / `not its completion status at exit` to confirm the sweep is closed.
issues.fix_summary:
All three swept, found by grep rather than memory (the same way the fifth cap-rule copy turned up). (1) code-review-standards.md check #13 - the dangerous one - now says a phase writes phase/status as its first act after validate-in AND AGAIN at the exit, tells a reviewer to flag a skill that writes at only one end, and states explicitly "Do NOT flag the exit write as duplication of the entry write: the redundancy is deliberate and load-bearing", naming the 0.29.0 removal-and-revert so a fresh-eyes reviewer cannot drive it back in. (2) non-functional-requirements.md now reads "...as its first act after validate-in, AND AGAIN at the exit alongside the iterations bump and phase-done - two writers on purpose". (3) project-knowledge.md's 0.29.0 entry no longer describes the release as shipping the regression: it records that FR11 removed the exit write, that phase 5 caught it making state.md arbitrarily stale rather than reliably one phase behind, and that the user restored it (entry AND exit, floor = one phase behind, ceiling = live). Re-grepped every phrasing ("stay at the exit", "no longer sets", "not its completion", "at ENTRY, not", "sits after the work") across knowledge/docs/skills/README/commands/templates/cli - no fourth site, and coding-rules.md + docs/cli-contract.md + docs/flow.md were already correct from the previous round.

MADE DETERMINISTIC RATHER THAN LEFT AS PROSE, because this rule has now regressed once and the standards were about to cause it again: TestPhaseSkillsWriteOccupancyAtEntryAndExit asserts all three phase skills write the occupancy status in BOTH sections and scope the exit write away from a gate status; TestReviewStandardsDoNotInviteTheExitWriteRemoval asserts the standards still carry the do-not-flag instruction and have not reverted to the wording that invited the removal. Both verified to bite by reproducing the exact regressions.

issues.title: The restored §④ write is unscoped, so a decision-gate round can overwrite `waiting-for-user` with `reviewing`/`testing`
issues.description: `gogo-review` §④ and `gogo-test` §④ list their routes first - including "**decision gate**: log to `decisions.md`, set `state.md` `waiting-for-user` (resume: review), stop and ask" - and then say, unconditionally, "Update `state.md`: **`phase: review`, `status: reviewing`**, and bump `iterations`". Read sequentially by an LLM that does not treat "stop and ask" as terminal, the exit write lands AFTER the gate and clobbers `waiting-for-user` back to a working status. The consequence is not cosmetic: `waiting-for-user` is what makes `WaitingForInput()` true, puts the card in `⏸ K need you`, sets the red gate stripe, and keeps `/gogo:go` from rerunning a feature that is parked on a user answer. This is a re-introduction, not a new defect - the pre-0.28.0 text had the same shape - but the 0.29.0 text it replaced ("leave phase/status as they are") did not, so the restoration brings the ambiguity back, in a release whose entire thesis is that prose instructions get misread. `gogo-implement` §④ has no decision-gate route and is unaffected. **Round 05 re-check:** the scoping sentence "Never overwrite a gate status with the working status" is present in all three phase skills' section 4 and is pinned by TestPhaseSkillsWriteOccupancyAtEntryAndExit (green). It AGREES with this round's TEST-002 guard rather than fighting it: section 4 leaves a gate status alone, so a paused card stays paused, and move.go refuses to launch while it is - while a round that CONTINUES still writes phase/status at exit, so a resumed round moves the status on even if the entry write is skipped (the gate is leavable without a hand edit). Verified.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, prose. Scope the sentence to the routes that continue, in both skills: "On the routes that CONTINUE (loop back to ② or advance), update `state.md`: `phase: review`, `status: reviewing`, and bump `iterations: review=<n+1>`. A **decision gate** sets `waiting-for-user` and stops - do not overwrite it with the working status." Keep the "the redundancy IS the design" paragraph as it is.
issues.fix_summary: Scoped in all three phase skills (implement/review/test), not just the two the finding named: "Scope: only on the routes that CONTINUE. A route that parks the item at a user gate (a decision gate -> waiting-for-user, and for 4 a blocked hands-on check) has already written the status that matters ... Never overwrite a gate status with the working status - write phase/status here only when the round loops back to 2 or advances." It names WHY the gate status is the one a reader must not lose: the gate count, the card stripe, and the /gogo:go refusal that stops an unattended rerun. Guarded: the skills test fails if any of the three drops the scoping sentence (verified by removing it).

issues.title: The now-routine hand-off blink is documented in the code comment but nowhere the user reads

issues.title: The gate bounce branches on a raw `uat` SUBSTRING instead of the package's own `isUATReplan`, so it disagrees with the pill on the same card - and the whole branch is unpinned
issues.description:
TEST-002's fix is correct in placement and force-proof (verified by mutation, see review-05.md), but its MESSAGE is a second, unpinned copy of a user-visible rule. `cli/internal/tui/move.go:146-153` (decisionGateBounce) says: "<slug> is paused on <D> - answer it in decisions.md, then run `/gogo:resume <slug>` to continue". `cli/go.go:447-448` (runnableHint, the headless surface for the SAME status) says: "it's paused on a decision - resolve it and re-accept (-> plan-accepted) first." Those are two different unblocks, and move.go's own doc comment asserts the opposite: "The wording deliberately mirrors cmdGo's runnableHint(\"waiting-for-user\") so the board and the headless surface tell the user the same story." Only the phrase "paused on a decision" is shared; the ACTIONABLE half diverges. Which one is right also matters: for an item paused at review, following the headless advice literally (re-accept -> plan-accepted) rewinds it to the start of the pipeline. Second, concrete half. The same comment claims the mid-UAT re-plan is covered: "A mid-UAT re-plan parks on the same status with an `open-decision: UAT round N`, and the same answer applies: resolve it, then resume." `skills/gogo/SKILL.md:262-293` says otherwise - that round's record lives in `uat.md` (not decisions.md), and "only this re-acceptance flips the feature off `waiting-for-user`", landing through the normal plan-acceptance flow owned by the orchestrator. `/gogo:resume` (`commands/resume.md`) is documented to clear `open-decision` and re-enter at `resume:` - a different route from the gate the skill deliberately holds - and `/gogo:accept` explicitly REFUSES this status (`skills/gogo-accept/SKILL.md:49`). So on the UAT shape the card renders `paused on UAT round 2` and the refusal tells the user to answer it in a file the round was never written to. Per code-review-standards check #12, a user-visible rule stated in more than one place must be one constant with its call sites pinned; three of four copies of the cap rule had gone stale for exactly this reason, and this is a fresh second copy.

**ROUND 06 - a fix landed and it does NOT close this; severity raised to major.** `decisionGateBounce` (move.go:168-184) now branches with `strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(gate), "uat")` on the free-prose `open-decision`. Three things are wrong with that, all reproduced against the real code (fixtures logged, not asserted-by-hand):
(1) **FALSE POSITIVE - new damage, the mirror image of the defect being fixed.** `open-decision: "D4 - uat asked for a different header"` is a PLAIN decision gate whose correct exit IS `/gogo:resume`. The bounce now reads "answer it in **uat.md**, then **re-accept the adjusted plan**" - wrong file AND an action that does not apply. Meanwhile `pillLabel` on the same card renders `⏸ decision`. Verified output, both surfaces, one Feature.
(2) **It duplicates a discriminator that already exists 550 lines away and is contract-anchored.** `uatRound`/`isUATReplan` (model.go:1289-1320) is the package's single "is this a UAT re-plan" predicate; `docs/cli-contract.md:260-264` makes `open-decision: UAT round N` the documented value and `skills/gogo/SKILL.md:265` is its writer. The two predicates disagree on real inputs: `"UAT feedback - the header wraps"` (no round number) -> pill `⏸ decision`, bounce `uat.md`. This is exactly the "one user-visible rule stated in more than one place that is not a single producer" shape code-review-standards check #12 (added in THIS release) tells a reviewer to flag.
(3) **Zero coverage.** Deleting the entire two-line UAT branch leaves all 12 packages GREEN (`go test -count=1 ./...`, sandbox copy). The only test touching `decisionGateBounce` is authoring_test.go:367, which pins the DECISION arm only. Nothing bites if the branch is reverted, re-inlined, or inverted.
The original defect is also still reachable in the direction it was filed for: a UAT round recorded without the literal `uat` (e.g. `open-decision: "round 2 - the header wraps"`) still routes to decisions.md + `/gogo:resume`.

**ROUND 07 (fix verified in a sandbox copy, `/tmp/gogo-rev07`; every mutation gofmt+`go vet`-checked before running, `-count=1`, sandbox restored after each; `diff -rq` against the repo clean).** **FIXED - VERIFIED.** `decisionGateBounce` (move.go:206) now calls `isUATReplan(f)` (model.go:1344 = `f.WaitingForUser() && uatRound(f) > 0`). The predicate CANNOT disagree with the pill: `decisionGateBounce` is only reached under `if f.WaitingForUser()` (move.go:93) and `pillLabel`'s `case "waiting-for-user"` (model.go:1298) calls the SAME `isUATReplan`, and `WaitingForUser()` is exactly `Status == "waiting-for-user"` (contract.go:119) - so the two branch on one predicate over one status. The digit rule is sound for the contract shape: `skills/gogo/SKILL.md:265` writes `open-decision: UAT round N` and `stripComment`/`stripPlaceholder` (state.go:183/175) strip the trailing HTML comment, so `uatRound` sees a clean `UAT round N`. MUTATION: reverting the branch to `strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(gate), "uat")` is CAUGHT by all three assertions of `TestDecisionGateBounceNamesTheRightArtifact/a_decision_that_merely_mentions_uat`, including the pill-agreement assertion. One residual on `uatRound`'s LOOSENESS filed separately as REV-036 (nit) - it does not affect bounce-vs-pill agreement.
issues.proposed_solution: **AGENT-FIXABLE**, and there IS a deterministic answer already in the file. (1) Replace the substring test with the existing predicate: `if isUATReplan(f) { where, how = "uat.md", "re-accept the adjusted plan" }`. That kills the false positive (`uatRound` needs a digit after `uat`, so `"D4 - uat asked for..."` scores 0 and routes to decisions.md), makes the bounce agree with `pillLabel` BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by coincidence, and anchors the wording on the documented `UAT round N` contract instead of on free prose. (2) Pin it: a table test over at least `"UAT round 1"` / `"D4 - uat asked for a different header"` / `"D3"` / `"none"` asserting the artifact AND the exit clause, plus an agreement assertion that `pillLabel` and `decisionGateBounce` never disagree about the gate flavour (that one cannot be escaped by re-inlining either side). Score it by deleting the branch: the suite must go red. (3) The residual - an orchestrator that writes a UAT round WITHOUT the documented `UAT round N` literal - is then a single shared failure mode with the pill rather than two divergent ones, and is worth a skills-lint guard pinning the literal in skills/gogo/SKILL.md:265.

issues.title: The not-runnable guard was added to the ClassUnfinished arm only - the ClassInProgress arm still returns ActionGo for a non-runnable status, so the board launches what `gogo go` refuses
issues.description:
`cli/internal/tui/move.go:93` refuses on `f.WaitingForUser()` - one status literal - where the project already owns the rule as `orchestrator.RunnableStatus` (`internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:111`), whose doc says plainly "`awaiting-uat` and `waiting-for-user` are NOT runnable (the user's UAT gate / a paused decision)". Only half of that is now enforced on the board. Verified empirically in a sandbox copy of this tree: a work item whose `state.md` reads `phase: knowledge` / `status: awaiting-uat` with NO `report/report.md` on disk classifies `unfinished` through the REAL loader (contract.classify -> readyToShipStatus needs a report, contract.go:457/473), and `attemptActionForce(false,false)` then returns intent `/gogo:go <slug>` with an EMPTY bounce - for `m` and for `M`. The same holds when the stale phase still names a pipeline phase (`phase: test` + `status: awaiting-uat` -> ClassInProgress -> `/gogo:go`, empty bounce). That is TEST-002's exact shape one status over: the board offers to relaunch the pipeline on an item that is waiting for the user's UAT verdict, with only the spawned session's own prose gate (`commands/go.md`) between the keypress and the run - the mitigation TEST-002 explicitly refused to rely on. Reachability is LOWER than TEST-002's, which is why this is minor and not major: it needs an awaiting-uat item whose report bundle is missing (a hand-deleted `report/`, or phase 5 setting the status while the bundle write did not complete - the same 'state.md is written at a phase's exit' family this release exists to fix), whereas TEST-002's paused card was the NORMAL shape. Headless `gogo go` refuses this case correctly (cli/go.go:159), so the two surfaces disagree here too.

**ROUND 06 - half fixed, and the open half is now proven MAJOR.**
**What landed and works (re-derived, not taken on trust).** The guard at move.go:124-126 sits on the GO return after the accept routing. Mutation: deleting the three lines fails `TestNotRunnableStatusIsRefusedByName` in BOTH subtests (`awaiting-uat` AND `shipped`), and also fails an independent real-loader reproduction I wrote (a temp repo -> `contract.LoadRepo` -> `awaiting-uat` + no `report/report.md` -> class `unfinished` -> `m`), for both `phase: knowledge` and `phase: plan`. The accept route survives: `awaiting-plan-acceptance` through the real loader still returns `/gogo:accept <slug>`, and `M` cannot force past either. **The coordinator's self-reported "known gap" (that the awaiting-uat arm does not discriminate) is FALSE** - it does, and it is fully attributed.
**What is still open, verified end-to-end.** `classify()` derives ClassInProgress from the `phase:` line ALONE (`inProgressPhaseOrStatus`: phase in {implement,review,test} OR status in {implementing,reviewing,testing}), and the `case contract.ClassInProgress:` arm (move.go:131-135) has NO RunnableStatus check. So the exact defect this issue was filed for survives whenever the phase line names a build phase - which is the state THIS WHOLE FEATURE exists to describe (a lagging `phase:` line; `· state lags`). Reproduced on a real repo fixture (`phase: review` + `status: awaiting-uat`, no report):
  - `gogo go x` -> REFUSES, exit 1: "feature \"x\" is \"awaiting-uat\" - not runnable here. it's at the UAT gate - run /gogo:done to ship..."
  - board `m` on the same card -> `/gogo:go x`, **empty bounce**, launch confirm opens (and the confirm-default convention seeds `true`, so a bare Enter launches it)
  - `gogo status` on the same card prints `WAIT  in-progress  review  awaiting-uat`
Every display surface says the user is holding the card while `m` launches it. That contradicts the fix's own comment - "cmdGo keys on the same predicate, so board and CLI refuse alike" - which is false for this arm: `cmdGo` (go.go:159) checks RunnableStatus unconditionally, with no class involvement at all. Same hole for the ACCEPT route: `phase: test` + `status: awaiting-plan-acceptance` classifies in-progress and returns `/gogo:go x`, not `/gogo:accept x`. The test cannot catch any of this because BOTH its fixtures hard-set `Class: contract.ClassUnfinished`.

**ROUND 07 (fix verified in a sandbox copy, `/tmp/gogo-rev07`; every mutation gofmt+`go vet`-checked before running, `-count=1`, sandbox restored after each; `diff -rq` against the repo clean).** **FIXED - VERIFIED, and the round-06 proposed fix was WRONG.** The shipped placement (the guard duplicated into `ClassUnfinished` move.go:125 and `ClassInProgress` move.go:141, leaving `ClassReadyToShip` alone) is correct. I re-derived all of it: (a) MUTATION, guard #0 removed -> CAUGHT, 2 subtests (`TestNotRunnableStatusIsRefusedByName/awaiting-uat_(unfinished)` + `/shipped_(unfinished)`), each 'returned go with an EMPTY bounce'. (b) MUTATION, guard #1 removed -> CAUGHT, 2 tests (`.../awaiting-uat_on_a_LAGGING_phase_line_(in-progress)` and `TestFooterChipMatchesWhatMActuallyDoes/uat_gate_on_a_lagging_phase_line`). So neither copy is redundant and neither is unpinned - this is NOT a REV-002/012/016/031-shaped drift pair: both copies are independently mutation-caught, so a divergence fails the suite. (c) MUTATION, both copies removed and ONE hoisted above `switch f.Class` (the round-06 proposal) -> CAUGHT by `TestAttemptActionGuards` (tui_test.go:165) and `TestForceMoveClaimsOverrideOnlyWhenItOverrode/ready_card_focused,_no_selection` (plans_view_test.go:851): a ready card's legal status IS `awaiting-uat`, so the hoist refuses the ship. The author's counter-evidence reproduces exactly; the round-06 proposal was wrong. (d) RE-DERIVED THROUGH THE REAL LOADER on a real repo (`t.TempDir()` + `.gogo/work/feature-x/` + `state.md` + `plan.md`, `contract.LoadRepo`), 4 shapes: `phase: knowledge`+`awaiting-uat` -> class `unfinished`, bounce names the UAT gate; `phase: review`+`awaiting-uat` -> class `in-progress`, same bounce (the round-06 hole, closed); `phase: test`+`awaiting-plan-acceptance` -> class `in-progress`, action `accept`, NO bounce (the accept route survives, and FR4a still precedes it at move.go:101); `phase: report`+`awaiting-uat`+`report/report.md` -> class `ready-to-ship`, action `done`, isShip=true. (e) NO THIRD ARM produces `ActionGo`. The two `intentFor(launch.ActionGo, ...)` sites in the switch are the only ones in `attemptActionForce`, `ClassShipped` returns a bounce, and the fall-through returns 'no legal move'. The other unattended producer, `autoPickupCmds` (pickup.go:113), is gated by `autoPickupReady` requiring `f.Status == "plan-accepted"` exactly (pickup.go:37) - a runnable status - plus `!f.PlanUnwritten`.
issues.proposed_solution: **AGENT-FIXABLE.** Hoist the check so it guards the DECISION, not one branch: put `if !orchestrator.RunnableStatus(f.Status) { return launch.Intent{}, false, notRunnableBounce(f) }` immediately before the `switch f.Class` - after the `f.WaitingForUser()` gate and after `planReadinessBounce`, but the accept route must then move above it (or be expressed as `if f.Status == "awaiting-plan-acceptance" { accept }` ahead of the runnable check) so the legal ACCEPT for a deliberately-not-runnable status is preserved - that is the arm the first, broad attempt swallowed, and it must stay green. That single placement makes the board key on exactly what `cmdGo` keys on, for every class, and lets the comment's claim become true. Extend `TestNotRunnableStatusIsRefusedByName` to a matrix of (class x status) built through the REAL loader (write state.md into a t.TempDir repo and call contract.LoadRepo) rather than hand-setting `Class`, covering at least: in-progress+awaiting-uat, in-progress+awaiting-plan-acceptance (must ACCEPT), in-progress+reviewing (must GO), unfinished+awaiting-uat, unfinished+plan-accepted (must GO). Score it by deleting the guard: every not-runnable row must go red.

issues.title: A stale ready-ship selection still launches `/gogo:done` on a card that has since moved to a user gate - `m` on a paused card, which the new bounce's own text promises never happens
issues.description:
The new gate check sits at `move.go:93`, AFTER the selection branch at `move.go:42-60`, which returns a merged/single `/gogo:done` intent before any guard runs. `m.selected` is keyed by featureKey and is cleared only on a launch or a ship-form cancel (`update.go:511`, `update.go:557`) - never on an fsnotify reload - while the card's selection TICK is filtered by class at render time (`view.go:613`: `f.Class == ClassReadyToShip && m.selected[...]`), and there is no selection count anywhere else on the board (`selectedSlugs()` has no non-test caller). So a selection that has gone stale is completely invisible. Verified in a sandbox copy: select the fixture's ready card (`awaiting-uat`), then move it to a mid-UAT re-plan lock (`status: waiting-for-user`, `open-decision: UAT round 2`, in-progress class - exactly what skills/gogo/SKILL.md:264-271 prescribes when the user raises UAT issues); the card then renders `⏸ re-planning · UAT 2` with NO tick, and `attemptActionForce(false,false)` returns `{Action:done Command:/gogo:done ready}` with an EMPTY bounce. With the confirm-default convention (a forward move seeds `confirm: true`, so a bare Enter submits) that is one keypress plus Enter from spawning `/gogo:done` on an item the user is mid-re-planning. Bounded by two things - the confirm names the real command, and the spawned `/gogo:done` requires `awaiting-uat` - but the second is the prose enforcement TEST-002 rejected, and the new refusal string asserts the opposite in the user's face: "(a paused card is never relaunched by m or M)". Minor rather than major because it needs a select-then-gate sequence and the confirm still shows the command; it is nonetheless the closest of this round's findings to TEST-002 itself.

**ROUND 06 - VERIFIED, and the mutation score re-derived independently (3/3).** `selectableForShip` (model.go:779) is quoted by all three surfaces - `selectedFeatures` (model.go:786), `renderCard`'s tick (view.go:613) and `toggleSelect` (update.go:305). Each reverted to its own literal, one at a time, in a sandbox copy, gofmt/vet-clean before each run: (a) `selectedFeatures` -> 3 assertion failures incl. "stale selection shipped ... with no bounce"; (b) `renderCard` -> "renderCard still marks a reclassified card as selected" with the rendered card printed; (c) `toggleSelect` -> "space armed a card at a decision gate" + "refused silently". All three caught, suite restored green after each. **The bypass is closed on the REAL path, not only in the fixture:** an independent reproduction (temp repo -> `contract.LoadRepo` -> select a genuinely ready card -> rewrite state.md to `waiting-for-user` + `open-decision: UAT round 1` -> `m.reload()`) confirms `m.selected` survives the reload (the `reloadMsg` handler at update.go:97-119 never clears it, by design), the card drops out AT THE READ, and `m`/`M` then fall through to the gate bounce. No fourth surface carries its own literal: `move.go:69` and `move.go:136` are the FOCUSED-card ship route and the class switch (routing, not selection membership) - judged acceptable, though quoting the predicate at :69 would cost nothing. Residual filed as REV-033.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, and the cheapest fix is at the read: have `selectedFeatures()` (model.go:767) return only cards that are STILL `ClassReadyToShip`, matching what `view.go:613` renders - one predicate for both, so the selection can never mean something the board is not showing. Then either drop the stale keys on reload or leave them harmless. If a silent drop feels wrong, bounce instead: when a selected key resolves to a card that is no longer ready, refuse and name it ("<slug> left the ready column (<status>) - press space to re-select"). Add a test: select a ready card, flip it to `waiting-for-user`, assert `m` bounces and builds no intent. Once fixed, the parenthetical in decisionGateBounce becomes true and can stay.

issues.description:

Neither covered the work item's OWN `plan.md` - the document review reviews against and, per the pipeline, the one phase 5 regenerates the report from. Three stale statements are still there. (Phase 5 owns this write ...)" - following it re-writes the superseded rule back into the knowledge base, which is precisely the self-reverting mechanism REV-021 flagged in code-review-standards. (`plan.md:690` repeats it inside a quoted round-2 note; lower stakes, but the same sentence.) Separately, the as-built section's "Folded in on the user's fix-now call at 4" bullet (plan.md:32) still lists TEST-001 only: TEST-002's decision-gate guard - a new user-visible refusal, a new production function and two new tests - and TEST-003 are recorded in adjustments.md and drawn in charts/flow.mmd, but not in the plan's shipped-vs-planned narrative, so the report regenerated from it will not mention them.

**ROUND 06 - three of the exit-write sites corrected, TWO items left.** Verified fixed: `plan.md:21-24` now records the removal-and-restoration and "belt and braces"; `plan.md:40` now reads "at entry AND AGAIN at exit - two writers on purpose"; `plan.md:805` (the Changes checklist phase 5 follows) now reads "at entry AND AGAIN at exit - two writers on purpose, because one of them is an LLM following prose". Still open:
(1) **The fourth site under `.gogo/work/**` is real and it is an INSTRUCTION, not narrative.** `plan.md:691`, inside the round-02 blockquote, still says "**Carried to ⑤:** ... and add *a phase writes its occupancy status at entry, not its completion status at exit*". `plan.md` now CONTRADICTS ITSELF about which rule phase 5 should write (:805 vs :691), which is the same self-reverting mechanism REV-021/REV-028 were filed for. A repo-wide grep for the exact phrasings (`at ENTRY, not`, `not its completion status at exit`) across `.gogo/ docs/ skills/ README.md templates/ commands/ cli/` finds only: plan.md:315 (FR11's PLANNED heading - correct to leave, it is the as-planned contract and the as-built section carries the delta), plan.md:691 (this one), report/report.md:436 (REV-024), adjustments.md:164 and :272 (historical log entries - correct to leave), and the review artifacts. So: one genuine fourth site.
(2) **The fold-in bullet was not extended.** `plan.md:33` still lists TEST-001 only. TEST-002 (`decisionGateBounce` + the guard), TEST-003, and now round 06's own production changes (`selectableForShip`, `notRunnableBounce`, the gate-bounce artifact branch, `TestStaleSelectionCannotShip`, `TestNotRunnableStatusIsRefusedByName`) appear NOWHERE in plan.md - grep for those symbols returns zero hits - so the planned-vs-shipped table phase 5 regenerates from it will not mention them.

issues.title: The control-pair scoring technique this round needed is sound but is not recorded in test-strategy.md, whose rule #7 prescribes a different method for a guard-only change
issues.description:
TEST-003 hardened a guard (whitespace-normalising a phrase match) rather than fixing production behaviour, so the usual "revert the fix, expect a failure" score is meaningless - the guard cannot fail while the defect it watches for is absent. The developer scored it with a CONTROL PAIR instead: inject the defect (the forbidden phrase reintroduced WRAPPED across a line break) and run the suite twice, once with the hardened guard and once with the raw one. I reproduced both legs independently in a sandbox copy of this tree: hardened + wrapped phrase -> TestReviewStandardsDoNotInviteTheExitWriteRemoval FAILS with the expected message; raw + wrapped phrase -> PASSES. With the clean baseline as the third leg, that is a complete detector score - sensitivity (defect present, fix in place -> fires), attribution (defect present, fix reverted -> silent, so the failure is caused by the normalisation and nothing else) and specificity (defect absent -> green). It is sound, and strictly stronger for this shape than test-strategy.md's rule 7 ("use a two-part mutation: weaken the guard AND introduce the defect, then check something else still bites"), which answers a different question - whether some OTHER assertion covers the gap - and would have scored this change as unverifiable. issues.title: The footer key-chip still advertises `[m] go` on cards whose `m` now bounces - four verified cases, two of them created this round
issues.description:
`footerChips` (view.go:814-839) picks the chip from `f.Class` alone. It was written for exactly this reason - its own comment says offering an affordance that bounces is "the same 'the board says one thing and does another' defect in miniature" - and it handles the plan-readiness case (`[m] ✗ plan not written`). Round 05's decision gate and round 06's not-runnable guard both added new `m` refusals WITHOUT updating it. Verified by driving `footerChips` and `attemptActionForce` over the same Feature, with two clean controls:
  - unfinished + `awaiting-uat` (no report) -> chip `[m] go`, bounce "x is at the UAT gate..." **LIES**
  - unfinished + `done` -> chip `[m] go`, bounce "x is done - not a runnable status..." **LIES**
  - unfinished + `aborted` -> chip `[m] go`, bounce "x is aborted - no move (illegal)" **LIES**
  - in-progress + `waiting-for-user` (D3) -> chip `[m] go`, bounce "x is paused on D3..." **LIES** (this arm entered in round 05)
  - in-progress + `implementing` -> chip `[m] go`, no bounce (control, correct)
  - unfinished + `plan-accepted` -> chip `[m] go`, no bounce (control, correct)
This is the feature's own thesis inverted: the board narrates a move it will refuse.

**ROUND 07 (fix verified in a sandbox copy, `/tmp/gogo-rev07`; every mutation gofmt+`go vet`-checked before running, `-count=1`, sandbox restored after each; `diff -rq` against the repo clean).** **PARTIALLY FIXED - REOPENED. Two verified lies remain and one of the two new arms is unpinned.** I swept the chip against `attemptActionForce` over the FULL cross product (4 classes x 12 statuses x PlanUnwritten true/false = 96 shapes) and found exactly two disagreements, both on `footerChips`' `ClassInProgress` arm (view.go:843-851), which is a 3-case copy of the `ClassUnfinished` arm's 5 cases - the same asymmetric-duplication shape REV-026 had:

The `ClassInProgress` arm has no `awaiting-plan-acceptance` case, so it falls to `!RunnableStatus`. The user is told a legal move is illegal.
  (2) **The chip promises `[m] go` where FR8 bounces.** class `in-progress` + status `plan-accepted` + `PlanUnwritten` -> chips `[m] go`, `m` bounces 'demo is plan-accepted but its plan.md is not written (no plan.md on disk yet) - nothing to build; re-plan it with `gogo plan demo`'. The `ClassInProgress` arm has no `planUnready` case; the `ClassUnfinished` arm does (view.go:829).
  (3) **The `ClassUnfinished` arm's new `✗ not runnable` chip is UNPINNED.** MUTATION: reverting view.go:837-839 to `c = append(c, chip("[m] go"))` leaves the WHOLE suite GREEN - i.e. the original REV-030 defect (`unfinished` + `awaiting-uat` advertising `[m] go`) can be restored with no test failing. `TestFooterChipMatchesWhatMActuallyDoes`'s table has no unfinished+not-runnable row (its only unfinished row is `waiting-for-user`, which hits the `WaitingForUser` case first). This is test-strategy variant 14 / code-review-standards #11(b) verbatim - one of the two arms the fix claims to have closed has no test that bites. (The `ClassInProgress` arm IS pinned: the same mutation there is CAUGHT.)
  Also unpinned but harmless: removing EITHER `✗ paused` case leaves the suite green, because the card then falls to `✗ not runnable` - still a refusal, so the test's outcome-level assertion cannot tell them apart (standards #11: name the exact reason).

If two switches are kept, add the missing `planUnready` and `awaiting-plan-acceptance` cases to the `ClassInProgress` arm. issues.title: `notRunnableBounce` claims to mirror `runnableHint` and already disagrees with it on `done`; the empty-status arm emits a malformed sentence; the pair is unpinned
issues.description:
move.go:154-166's doc comment says "It mirrors cmdGo's runnableHint so board and CLI agree (REV-026)". Walked arm by arm against go.go:436-455 and go.go:152-162:
  - `awaiting-uat`: agrees (the board's is better - it names the slug in the command).
  - `shipped`/`aborted`: board says "<slug> is <status> - no move (illegal)"; the CLI does not refuse at all - `TerminalStatus` (go.go:153) REAPS the session and exits **0** with "nothing to run; reaped any tracked session". Different outcome, not just different words; acceptable for a board (it cannot reap from `m`) but the comment's claim is wrong.
  - **`done`: outright drift.** `TerminalStatus` includes `done`, and `runnableHint` folds `done` into "it's already shipped."; `notRunnableBounce` lists only `shipped`/`aborted`, so `done` falls to the generic default: "x is done - not a runnable status; `/gogo:go` needs plan-accepted, implementing, reviewing or testing". Verified output. A legacy `status: done` item with no report classifies unfinished, so the arm is reachable.
  - **empty status**: "x is  - not a runnable status; ..." - double space, and the refusal names no value, against the Diagnosability bar's "a limit must name its number" spirit. Reachable: a written plan.md plus a state.md with no `status:` line is not `Authoring()` (that needs `PlanUnwritten`), so it reaches this arm.
Nothing pins the pair - `notRunnableBounce` appears in no test outside `TestNotRunnableStatusIsRefusedByName`'s two substring checks, and `runnableHint` is never compared to it. REV-002 / REV-012 / REV-016 were all this exact shape (a hand-copied rule that went stale in 3 of 4 places).

**ROUND 07 (fix verified in a sandbox copy, `/tmp/gogo-rev07`; every mutation gofmt+`go vet`-checked before running, `-count=1`, sandbox restored after each; `diff -rq` against the repo clean).** **ARMS ALIGNED, BUT THE ALIGNMENT TARGET IS DEAD CODE AND THE FIX INTRODUCED A FALSE STATEMENT. Reopened.** The two concrete defects ARE fixed and pinned: MUTATION removing `done` from the terminal arm -> CAUGHT by `TestBounceArmsMatchRunnableHint`; MUTATION removing the `case ""` arm -> CAUGHT (both the double-space and the 'no status on disk' assertions). Three things are still wrong:
  (1) **The board now tells a falsehood about an ABORTED card.** `notRunnableBounce` (move.go:166) folds `aborted` into `case "shipped", "done", "aborted"` and returns 'x is **already shipped** - no move (illegal)'. An aborted work item was never shipped - there is no changelog entry to look for. Before this round the same card read 'x is aborted - not a runnable status; ...', which was generic but TRUE; the fix traded a correct message for a wrong one, and `TestBounceArmsMatchRunnableHint` asserts the wrong string (`want the terminal wording runnableHint uses`) for `aborted`. Per the Diagnosability bar a message that misstates the state is worse than a generic one.
  (2) **The arm it was aligned TO is unreachable.** `runnableHint` has exactly ONE production call site, go.go:160 - and go.go:152 returns FIRST for `orchestrator.TerminalStatus` (shipped/done/aborted) with a different sentence and **exit 0**: 'gogo go: x is done - nothing to run; reaped any tracked session.' So `runnableHint`'s `case "shipped", "done", "aborted"` is dead from the CLI's perspective, and the board was matched to a string the user never sees from `gogo go`. That is code-review-standards #11(c) - the test passes for a weaker reason than it claims.
  (3) **It is still two hand-written prose copies in two packages, with no shared producer.** `TestBounceArmsMatchRunnableHint` never calls `runnableHint` (it cannot - `runnableHint` is in package `main`); it asserts hard-coded literals, so its NAME and doc comment claim a cross-surface guarantee its assertions do not provide. Proof the pair is unlinked: the generic arms ALREADY disagree - for an unknown status the board says '...not a runnable status; `/gogo:go` needs plan-accepted, implementing, reviewing or testing' while `runnableHint`'s `default` says 'run /gogo:plan and accept a plan first.'
  **JUDGEMENT ASKED FOR: yes, a shared producer is warranted, not a test.** This is the fifth occurrence of the shape in one feature (REV-002/012/016/031), and the project's own rules mandate it: `coding-rules.md:102` ('a user-visible rule stated in more than one place is ONE constant... then pin the wirings, not just the producer') and `code-review-standards.md:76` (#12). The precedent shipped in THIS release: `orchestrator.CapRuleClause` / `CapSweepRemedy` / `CapRefusal`. `internal/orchestrator` already holds `RunnableStatus`/`TerminalStatus` and is already imported by both `main` and `tui`, so the move has no import problem.
issues.proposed_solution: **AGENT-FIXABLE.** Move the per-status refusal sentences into `internal/orchestrator` next to `RunnableStatus`/`TerminalStatus` (e.g. `orchestrator.NotRunnableReason(status, slug string) string`), have BOTH `notRunnableBounce` and `runnableHint` quote it, and pin the wirings (assert each surface's rendered output contains the produced string, per test-strategy variant 8). While doing it: split `aborted` out of the shipped arm ('x was aborted - no move'), and decide deliberately whether the board should mirror `gogo go`'s ACTUAL terminal path (go.go:152, exit 0 + reap) rather than `runnableHint`'s dead arm. Then fix the test's name/doc so it no longer claims a cross-package guarantee it cannot make.
