issues.title: A stale ship selection is FILTERED, not cleared, so it resurrects itself when the card becomes ready again - verified across a full UAT loop
issues.description:
REV-027's fix deliberately filters at the READ (`selectedFeatures`) and leaves the key in `m.selected`, because "selection is not cleared on reload by design". The consequence is that a selection is SUSPENDED, not dropped. Reproduced against the real loader on a temp repo, three reloads:
  t0  `awaiting-uat` + report -> ready-to-ship, selected=1, card shows ✓
  t1  UAT feedback -> `waiting-for-user` -> unfinished, selected=0, ✓ gone (the fix working)
  t2  the rerun finishes -> `awaiting-uat` again -> ready-to-ship, **selected=1, ✓ back**, and `m` returns `/gogo:done shipme` (isShip=true, empty bounce) with no keystroke having re-armed it.
The ✓ does reappear, so it is visible rather than silent - but the cockpit is designed to stay open across exactly this loop (fsnotify reload, auto-pickup), a UAT round is hours, and `startFormOverriding` seeds the confirm `true`, so a bare Enter on the reappeared selection ships. "Selection survives a refresh" is the intended property; "selection survives leaving and re-entering ready-to-ship" is not, and no test pins either.

**ROUND 07 (fix verified in a sandbox copy, `/tmp/gogo-rev07`; every mutation gofmt+`go vet`-checked before running, `-count=1`, sandbox restored after each; `diff -rq` against the repo clean).** **FIXED - VERIFIED for the resurrect path.** `pruneSelection` (model.go:772) is called at the top of `rebuild()` (model.go:675), and `rebuild()` runs from `reload()` (model.go:724), so it fires on every fsnotify reload. MUTATION: removing the `m.pruneSelection()` call is CAUGHT by all three assertions of `TestStaleSelectionDoesNotResurrect`, including 'm shipped [shipme] from a resurrected selection'. The resurrect is closed. A DIFFERENT failure direction the fix opened is filed as REV-035 (minor): the prune keys on ABSENCE from `m.repo.Features`, so a transiently degraded read drops a legitimate selection permanently.
issues.proposed_solution: **AGENT-FIXABLE**, one loop. In `Model.reload()` (model.go:710-724), after `m.rebuild()`, prune keys whose feature is no longer selectable: build the set of `featureKey(f)` for features passing `selectableForShip`, and `delete` any `m.selected` key not in it. That keeps the intended property exactly (a card that is still ready keeps its ✓ across any number of reloads) while making a de-selection permanent, so a selection is dropped once rather than suspended. Extend `TestStaleSelectionCannotShip` with the t0->t1->t2 loop above, asserting selected=0 at t2; deleting the prune must turn it red.

issues.title: pruneSelection keys on ABSENCE, so a transiently degraded read silently drops a legitimate ship selection - permanently
issues.description:
`pruneSelection` (model.go:772) builds a `live` set from `m.repo.Features` and deletes every `m.selected` key NOT in it. That treats 'the card was not in this load' as 'the card is not selectable', but the contract reader is deliberately LENIENT: `LoadRepo` swallows the `os.ReadDir` error (contract.go:260) so an unreadable `.gogo/work` yields ZERO features with no error; `LoadProject` skips such a source (contract.go:287); and `parseStateFile` returns an empty Feature for a missing/truncated/comment-broken file (state.go:23) so a mid-write `state.md` classifies `unfinished`. Any of those makes a genuinely-ready card momentarily absent-or-reclassified, and the entry is then gone for good - the card comes back on the next good reload, the user's selection does not.

VERIFIED THROUGH THE REAL LOADER, on a real repo on disk (`t.TempDir()` + `.gogo/work/feature-shipme/` + `report/report.md` + `plan.md`, loaded with `contract.LoadProject`, real `NewWorkspaceAll` model, real `m.reload()`): select the ready card (`selectedFeatures`=1) -> rewrite `state.md` truncated (no `status:` line yet) -> `m.reload()` gives `class="unfinished"`, `m.selected=map[]` -> restore the full `state.md` -> `m.reload()` -> `selectedFeatures`=0. The card is ready again and armed by nobody. Also reproduced with the coarser trigger (`m.repo = &contract.Repo{}` for one reload).

Why this is the same family REV-027/REV-033 are about, in the other direction: a selection the user MADE and can no longer find is as confusing as one they did not make, and nothing announces it. It also violates the project's own reader principle - `non-functional-requirements.md:47` 'Prefer degrading to MISSING over degrading to WRONG', where every defensive-reader decision is chosen so a degraded read can only lose a VALUE. `pruneSelection` is the first place a degraded read causes a permanent, silent MUTATION of user intent.

Honest reachability: the 300 ms fsnotify debounce (`watch.go:14`) coalesces bursts, so catching a mid-write `state.md` is a narrow window; a source on a slow/removable mount, a `git checkout` that swaps `.gogo/work/`, or a source removed and re-added in the config tab are the wider ones. Harm is bounded (a merged ship silently carries fewer slugs, or `d` bounces 'only ready cards can ship') - hence minor, not major.
issues.proposed_solution:
**AGENT-FIXABLE. Note the obvious narrowing does NOT work** - I tried it: pruning only keys that are PRESENT-but-not-selectable still drops the mid-write case, because a truncated `state.md` leaves the feature present and classified `unfinished`. Two options that do work:
(a) **Make the drop non-silent** (cheapest, and it satisfies the Diagnosability bar): have `pruneSelection` return the dropped slugs and set `m.status` ('dropped N card(s) from the ship selection: <slugs> - they are no longer ready'). A legitimate prune is then explained and a spurious one is visible instead of invisible, which is the whole point of REV-027/REV-033.
(b) **Prune only on a POSITIVE transition**: drop a key only when the card is present AND its status is a definite non-ready one (`WaitingForUser()`, `TerminalStatus`, or a runnable in-flight status) - never on an empty/unknown status, which is exactly the reader's 'degraded to missing' signal.
Test: extend `TestStaleSelectionDoesNotResurrect` with a third leg that reloads through a degraded read (empty `Repo`, and a truncated `state.md` through `LoadRepo`) and asserts the selection SURVIVES; keep the existing resurrect leg so both directions bite.

issues.title: uatRound's digit rule is looser than the contract it is anchored on - it reads the first integer ANYWHERE after "uat"
issues.description:
Asked to check that `uatRound`'s digit rule matches what the orchestrator actually writes: it does for the contract shape, but it is strictly looser. `skills/gogo/SKILL.md:265` writes exactly `open-decision: UAT round N` and `docs/cli-contract.md:262` documents it, yet `uatRound` (model.go:1315) lowercases the value, finds the first `uat` ANYWHERE, and returns the first whole integer that follows it ANYWHERE. So `open-decision: D4 - uat asked for a v2 header` yields round 2, and `isUATReplan` is true: the bounce sends the user to `uat.md` and tells them to 're-accept the adjusted plan' for what is a plain D4 whose real exit is `/gogo:resume`. This is the SAME false-positive class REV-025 was filed for, one notch narrower (it now needs a digit, so REV-025's own regression case `"D4 - uat asked for a different header"` is correctly rejected).

Not a regression and not a bounce-vs-pill disagreement: `pillLabel` has always used `uatRound`, so the pill mislabels the identical card ('⏸ re-planning · UAT 2'). The REV-025 fix's agreement property holds; this is the residual looseness of the shared predicate, now visible on one more surface. Filed as a nit because it needs a digit inside a decision title that also contains the word uat.
issues.proposed_solution: **AGENT-FIXABLE, one regexp.** Anchor `uatRound` on the shape the contract actually writes rather than on free prose: `^\s*uat\s+round\s+(\d+)` (case-insensitive) against the trimmed `OpenDecision`. That still reads `UAT round 10` whole (the multi-digit case the current scanner was written for), and it makes the predicate a parse of the documented contract instead of a heuristic over a title - the same 'anchor on the contract, not the prose' move REV-025 made one level up. Add the false-positive row (`D4 - uat asked for a v2 header` -> decisions.md, pill `⏸ decision`) to `TestDecisionGateBounceNamesTheRightArtifact` so it bites.
